extracted.intended_audience: small businesses, telecom providers, licensees, and legal/industry stakeholders interacting with FCC regulatory processes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance within an FCC Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA) describing how the Commission and SBA classify small entities in various telecommunications industries (wired, wireless, auctioned services), which data sources and NAICS codes are used, and auction-specific small/very small business definitions and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard for Wired Telecommunications Carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for Wired Telecommunications Carriers classifies firms having 1,500 or fewer employees as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited repeatedly (see 13 CFR § 121.201, NAICS Code 517311). U.S. Census Bureau 2017 data are used to estimate number of firms (e.g., 3,054 firms in 2017; 2,964 with fewer than 250 employees). The available Census data may not provide a more precise estimate of the number of firms that meet the SBA size standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard for Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA size standard for this industry classifies a business as small if it has 1,500 or fewer employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited to 13 CFR § 121.201, NAICS Code 517312 (as of 10/1/22, NAICS Code 517112). Uses U.S. Census Bureau 2017 Economic Census employment size data (e.g., 2,893 firms in 2017; 2,837 with fewer than 250 employees). Commission uses these figures to estimate that most providers can be considered small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of U.S. Census Bureau NAICS codes and Economic Census data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission relies on U.S. Census Bureau NAICS definitions and 2017 Economic Census tables (employment size, revenues/receipts) to identify industries and estimate number/size of firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NAICS 517311 Wired Telecommunications Carriers; NAICS 517312 Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite); NAICS 517919 All Other Telecommunications. Specific table IDs cited (e.g., EC1700SIZEEMPFIRM, EC1700SIZEREVFIRM). The FRFA notes limitations in the available Census data for precisely identifying firms that meet SBA size standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closest-industry rule when no specific SBA/Commission size standard exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission or SBA has not developed a size standard specifically applicable to a particular service (e.g., Local Exchange Carriers, Interexchange Carriers, Operator Service Providers, Other Toll Carriers), the Commission uses the closest applicable industry SBA small business size standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Local Exchange Carriers, Incumbent LECs, Competitive LECs, Interexchange Carriers, Operator Service Providers, and Other Toll Carriers are compared to Wired Telecommunications Carriers as the 'closest industry' with an SBA standard. The text repeats that Wired Telecommunications Carriers is the closest industry with an SBA small business size standard for many wireline categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction-specific designated entity and bidding-credit small business rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For frequency bands subject to auction, the Commission's small business size standards often govern eligibility for bidding credits and installment payments; these criteria may be based on average gross revenues and are set in the competitive bidding rules and designated entities sections of Part 27 (or the applicable Part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRFA notes that bidding credits and installment payment eligibility may be available to several types of small businesses (small, very small, entrepreneur) pursuant to rules adopted for a specific auction and referenced in Part 27 subparts (Subparts D–Q). Citations: 47 CFR §§ 27.201 – 27.1601 and band-specific designated entity sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average gross revenue thresholds for 'small' and 'very small' bidders in certain auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: In some auctions the Commission defines 'small business' and 'very small business' by average gross revenues for the preceding three years (e.g., 'small' ≤ $40 million; 'very small' ≤ $15 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit examples: 1670–1675 MHz service band auction and Broadband PCS auctions used these thresholds. References: 47 CFR § 27.906(a) (1670–1675 MHz) and 47 CFR § 24.720(b) (Broadband PCS). The FRFA notes which blocks/historical auctions employed these definitions and that winning bidders may or may not have claimed small status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission caveat about auction winners vs. in-service small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of winning bidders that claim to qualify as small businesses at the close of an auction does not necessarily represent the number of small businesses currently in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission generally does not track subsequent business size unless assignments/transfers or unjust enrichment issues are implicated. Therefore auction outcomes are not definitive measures of currently operating small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission data-collection limitations on employee counts for licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission does not collect data on the number of employees for licensees providing many services, and thus sometimes cannot estimate how many licensees with active licenses would qualify as small under the SBA size standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRFA repeatedly notes this limitation when discussing WCS, SMR, SMR licensees, Broadband PCS, and other categories—stating inability to estimate number of licensees meeting the SBA standard because employee-count data are not collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active licenses vs. number of licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of active licenses does not equate to the number of licensees; a licensee can hold one or more licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in context of FCC Universal Licensing System searches (e.g., counts of active licenses for Broadband PCS, SMR). This distinction affects how the Commission interprets counts returned by license searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification inclusions/exclusions for Fixed Local Service Providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed Local Service Providers include specified provider types (ILECs, CAPs, CLECs, Cable/Coax CLECs, Interconnected VoIP Providers, Non-Interconnected VoIP Providers, Shared-Tenant Service Providers, Audio Bridge Service Providers, and Other Local Service Providers); Local Resellers fall into another NAICS group and are not included in this industry data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRFA lists these provider types to clarify which providers are included when using the Wired Telecommunications Carriers/Fixed Local Service Provider classifications and notes that Local Resellers are excluded from that industry grouping in Census statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMR and other specific-service mapping to SBA standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For services such as Specialized Mobile Radio (SMR), 1670–1675 MHz services, Broadband PCS, and other specified bands, the FRFA maps those services to the closest SBA industry and applies the SBA small business size standard (commonly 1,500 or fewer employees) unless auction-specific revenue-based definitions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SMR licensees are treated as part of Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite) for SBA comparison; Commission uses U.S. Census and FCC Universal Service Monitoring Report data (e.g., SMR providers counted as 95 dispatch providers, Commission estimates all 95 have ≤1,500 employees). The FRFA repeats mapping pattern across multiple service types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Commission reports and searches to supplement Census data
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRFA uses Commission sources (Universal Service Monitoring Report, Universal Licensing System searches, FCC Auctions database, Industry Analysis Division reports) to supplement Census data when estimating numbers of providers and licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: Universal Service Monitoring Report Table 1.12; ULS searches for active licenses; FCC Auctions pages; Industry Analysis Division 'Internet Access Services: Status as of June 30, 2019.' The FRFA notes that these Commission-derived counts have interpretive caveats (e.g., license counts vs. licensee counts).
